correctness.rationale: The frozen condition is precisely cross-shore equality or disagreement in both coordinates. In the 3×3 culture grid a singleton has five compatible cultures; a distinct pair sharing a coordinate has the complementary two-point common-neighbor palette (whose common-neighbor palette in reverse is the original pair), and a pair sharing neither coordinate has the unique three-point permutation palette. This yields exactly 42 maximal oriented pairs, not 42 individual supports. Inclusion-exclusion for the two monochromatic-shore families and the permutation-triple family gives 9(5^a+5^b)+6·3^(a+b)−18(3^a+3^b)+9; the remaining disjoint family gives 18(2^a−2)(2^b−2). This verifies the formula for all positive shores, including a=1 or b=1 and the small 2×2 case. With a≤b and both tending to infinity, 5^a≤5^((a+b)/2)=o(3^(a+b)), and all other corrections and dominant-family intersections are lower order than 9·5^b+6·3^(a+b). Surjection error bounds show that the two dominant families actually use five and three cultures, respectively. Their weight ratio is (2/3)·3^(a−θb), giving both phases and the stated offset-dependent mixture.
residual_risks: Sampling is uniform over labelled frozen configurations, not the absorption law of the stochastic dynamics. A limiting ratio a/b=θ without further information about the offset does not specify mixture weights.

value.rationale: The first three-value, two-feature target goes beyond monochromatic or single compatible-pair supports. The natural unbalanced complete bipartite test case lets one identify two geometrically distinct types of typical frozen state and their exact transition, including nontrivial critical weights. It is an exact comparison for a defined frozen ensemble, not a claim about cultural evolution trajectories.
residual_risks: No extension to other feature/trait counts, sparse hosts, or the dynamically selected absorption ensemble is established.
